Chapter 6: Tackling Debt—Finding Relief and Building Momentum
Debt can really feel like a heavy shadow, always hanging around in the background, can’t it? For so many people, it’s not just about the amount they owe—it’s that constant, nagging worry. Will there ever be a way out?
The pressure builds up quietly. Maybe it shows up as sleepless nights, or that knot in your stomach every time the phone rings. If you’ve ever felt alone in this struggle, you’re definitely not. Debt is something millions face every day.
Let me share a story. There was someone who, after years of ignoring credit card statements, finally decided to face the pile. The first step? Just opening every envelope—even when it felt overwhelming. Each bill got listed out, and for the very first time, they could see the total. Sure, it was a big number, but somehow, seeing it all in one place made it less mysterious—and honestly, a whole lot less scary.
Here’s something a lot of people don’t realize: the hardest part is often just starting. Once you’ve named those debts, you can actually make a plan. Some folks find relief in the “debt snowball” method—paying off the smallest balance first, then rolling that payment into the next debt. Others go with the “avalanche” approach, tackling the highest interest rate first.
In the end, the method matters less than the sense of progress you feel. Every little win builds momentum. And with each paid-off account, you’ll notice the weight starts to lift, bit by bit.
One woman I know was juggling student loans and medical bills. She set up automatic payments for the minimums, then focused any extra cash on her smallest loan. She celebrated each milestone, no matter how small—a zero balance on a store card, a letter confirming a loan was paid off. Over time, those victories really added up, and her confidence grew along with them.
What’s become so clear is that shame and secrecy only make debt harder to manage. When you open up—maybe with a trusted friend, a partner, or even a financial counselor—the burden gets lighter. Sometimes, just saying that number out loud is enough to break the spell.
There’s no magic fix. But there is a path forward—one step at a time. And with each step, you’ll find that relief and momentum are a lot closer than they seemed.
